releaseNote.summary: Workflows can declare attributes.rowSecurity: role-keyed row rules, deny by default, that filter the instance list and single GET (and GetInstances/GetInstance tasks).

rowSecurity.description: A flow declares attributes.rowSecurity.rules (role-keyed row filters in the list-engine filter language, with $.context.Headers / QueryParameters / CurrentUser parameters and the $InstanceStarter / $InstanceBehalfOfStarter identity rules). There is no default: a flow with rowSecurity is deny by default, and 'role X sees everything' is an explicit unfiltered rule; a flow without it is unchanged. A caller sees the OR of the matched static rules' filters plus declared identity rules, ANDed with their own filter; a failed role resolution or any failed parameter yields no rows from that rule and never widens. The rule set is the flow's default version (sys-version-registry pointer) when set, else the latest, read with GetFlowAsync(domain, workflow, null) for instances of every version; a lookup failure other than 'no definition' denies the list and GET of every flow and returns the lookup error as is. Phase 1 filters only the instance list (including groupBy and aggregations) and the single GET (excluded answers the same 404 as missing, before the ETag); state/data/view/schema/master/history/internal functions and the GetInstanceData task are unfiltered, so the GET 404 is not a confidentiality boundary. Requires a gateway that strips or overwrites the role header and every header a rule reads; QueryParameters are client-controlled. Publish warnings (RS-W*) are log-only. Rolling the runtime back below this version while flows declare rowSecurity serves every row: remove rowSecurity first. Requires the runtime version that ships this entry and a vnext-schema release containing workflow.attributes.rowSecurity.

knownIssues.title: rowSecurity filters the instance list and single GET only; the state/data/view/schema/master/history/internal functions and the GetInstanceData task serve excluded instances by id, and GET 404 next to data 200 is an existence oracle.
knownIssues.workaround: Do not treat rowSecurity as an access boundary for an instance whose id the caller knows; enforce access to those functions at the gateway (authorize) until instance-addressed coverage ships.
